flashcards.back: "object" — a legacy JS representation bug.
"152" — 10 + 5 = 15, then 15 + "2" coerces to the string "152".

flashcards.front: JS event loop: microtasks vs macrotasks order
flashcards.back: The microtask queue (Promise.then, queueMicrotask) drains completely BEFORE the macrotask queue (setTimeout, I/O). Promise.resolve().then(...) always runs before setTimeout(..., 0).
var is function-scoped and hoisted as undefined; let/const are block-scoped with a Temporal Dead Zone (TDZ). const prevents re-assignment, NOT object/array mutation.
unknown is type-safe — it requires type narrowing before accessing properties or calling methods; any disables type checking completely.

flashcards.front: React: useRef vs useState re-render behavior
flashcards.back: useState triggers a re-render on update; useRef persists a mutable value across renders WITHOUT triggering a re-render.

flashcards.front: React: useEffect(fn, []) vs no dependency array
flashcards.back: useEffect(fn, []) runs once on mount; omitting the dependency array runs the effect after EVERY render.

flashcards.front: Why avoid array indices as React list keys when items reorder/delete?
flashcards.back: It breaks reconciliation and can associate component state with the wrong item. Keys should identify items, not their array positions.

flashcards.front: Java 8 HashMap: what happens when a bucket exceeds 8 colliding entries?
flashcards.back: With table capacity >= 64, the bucket converts from a linked list to a balanced Red-Black Tree, improving worst-case lookup from O(n) to O(log n).
If a.equals(b) is true, then a.hashCode() == b.hashCode() MUST hold (the reverse need not be true).

flashcards.front: Java: final vs finally vs finalize()
flashcards.back: final = constant/non-overridable; finally = cleanup block; finalize() = deprecated garbage-collection hook.

Checked (compile-time verified): IOException, SQLException, ClassNotFoundException. Unchecked (RuntimeException subclasses): NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException, ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException.

flashcards.front: Java exception thrown by Class.forName() when no definition is found?
flashcards.back: ClassNotFoundException — a checked exception thrown during dynamic class loading.
Heap (objects & instance variables, GC-managed); Stack (thread-local method frames & local primitives); Metaspace (Java 8+ replacement for PermGen; stores class metadata in native memory).
@Configuration, @EnableAutoConfiguration, and @ComponentScan.
@RestController = @Controller + @ResponseBody.

By default rolls back only on unchecked (RuntimeException/Error) exceptions, NOT checked exceptions unless rollbackFor = Exception.class is set. Self-invocation within the same class bypasses the AOP proxy.
Singleton (others: prototype, request, session). Singleton scope does not make a bean inherently thread-safe.
Constructor injection — makes required dependencies explicit, immutable and testable.
In CPython, only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time. Use threading/asyncio for I/O-bound tasks and multiprocessing for CPU-bound tasks.
def f(a=[]): a.append(1) shares the SAME list across calls because the default is created once at definition. Always default to None and initialize inside the function.
Generators (yield) produce values lazily with O(1) memory; list comprehensions materialize the full list in RAM.

flashcards.front: HTTP methods that are BOTH safe and idempotent
flashcards.back: GET and HEAD.
PUT is idempotent (full replacement); POST is neither safe nor inherently idempotent (create/trigger action).
401 Unauthorized = missing/invalid authentication; 403 Forbidden = authenticated identity but lacks permission.
502 Bad Gateway = gateway/proxy got an invalid response from upstream; 503 Service Unavailable; 504 Gateway Timeout.
429 Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded.

flashcards.front: Pattern to prevent double-debiting on retried POST /transfers
flashcards.back: Client-generated Idempotency-Key persisted with the transaction, so a repeated request has the same effect as one execution.
Manage distributed transactions via local transactions and compensating actions, instead of two-phase commit (2PC).
Closed -> Open -> Half-Open — trips open to stop cascading microservice failures.
OAuth 2.0 = authorization framework; OIDC = authentication/identity layer on OAuth 2.0; JWT = stateless signed token format (Header.Payload.Signature), signed not encrypted.

flashcards.front: REST vs SOAP vs GraphQL vs gRPC
flashcards.back: SOAP = XML + WSDL + WS-Security (legacy CBS); REST = JSON/HTTP resources; GraphQL = single endpoint avoiding over/under-fetching; gRPC = HTTP/2 + Protocol Buffers for low-latency inter-service calls.

CORS is a browser-enforced cross-origin access policy (not authentication). CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) exploits ambient credentials; defend with SameSite cookies, anti-CSRF tokens and origin checks.
Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (preserves invariants/constraints), Isolation (concurrent txns don't interfere), Durability (committed data survives crash via Write-Ahead Logging).

flashcards.front: Which ACID property is violated if a debit isn't rolled back after a failed credit?
flashcards.back: Atomicity — it guarantees all-or-nothing execution of a transaction.
No multi-valued or composite attributes — every cell holds a single indivisible (atomic) value.
In 1NF + no partial dependency (no non-prime attribute depending on part of a composite key). Automatically satisfied if the primary key is a single column.
In 2NF + no transitive dependency (non-prime -> non-prime). For X -> Y: X is a superkey OR Y is a prime attribute.
Stricter 3NF: for EVERY non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y, X must be a superkey / candidate key. Every determinant must be a candidate key.
Reading a row modified by another transaction that has NOT yet committed (and may later roll back).
Non-Repeatable Read = same row read twice yields different committed values. Phantom Read = re-running a predicate query returns a changed SET of rows.

flashcards.front: Isolation level preventing Dirty + Non-Repeatable Reads but allowing Phantoms (SQL-92)
flashcards.back: REPEATABLE READ (MySQL InnoDB default; InnoDB gap locks also prevent phantoms).
Prevents Dirty Reads; allows Non-Repeatable & Phantom Reads. Default in PostgreSQL/Oracle.
Prevents dirty, non-repeatable and phantom reads — highest isolation, lowest concurrency.
CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE, RENAME — schema definition, auto-committed.
SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE — data rows, rollback-able.
DCL (permissions): GRANT, REVOKE. TCL (transactions): COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT.
DELETE: DML, supports WHERE, logs each row, fires triggers, rollback-able. TRUNCATE: DDL, removes all rows fast, resets auto-increment, no WHERE. DROP: removes data AND table structure.

flashcards.front: How many clustered indexes per table?
flashcards.back: At most one — it determines the physical row order on disk (usually the primary key). A table can have multiple non-clustered indexes.
B+ Trees (default in PostgreSQL/MySQL/Oracle) support range queries (BETWEEN, <, >, ORDER BY). Hash indexes support only exact equality (=) in O(1).
An index on (a, b, c) helps queries on a, or a,b — NOT on b,c alone. Wrapping an indexed column in a function (e.g. WHERE YEAR(dt)=2026) breaks index usage.
OLTP = high-concurrency short transactional writes (normalized 3NF, core banking). OLAP = complex historical aggregations / multi-dimensional analytical queries (denormalized).
Star schema keeps dimension tables denormalized for faster query joins. Snowflake schema normalizes dimension tables to save storage.
Type 1 overwrites (no history); Type 2 adds a new row/version to preserve history (effective dates/current flag); Type 3 stores a limited previous value in extra field(s).
WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.
COUNT(*) counts all rows; COUNT(column) excludes NULLs. NULL is not equal to any value including NULL — use IS NULL.
Best/Avg O(n log n), Worst O(n^2), Space O(log n) for tail-recursive; unstable.
O(n log n) in all cases, space O(n); stable, divide-and-conquer, ideal for linked lists / external sort.
O(n log n) time, O(1) space; in-place, unstable; uses a binary heap.

flashcards.front: Which sorts bypass the O(n log n) comparison lower bound?
flashcards.back: Counting, Radix and Bucket sort — non-comparison sorts, O(n + k).
O(log n); requires a sorted / monotonic search space.
BFS uses a Queue (shortest path in unweighted graphs); DFS uses a Stack/recursion (cycle detection, topological sort). Both are O(V+E) with an adjacency list.
Dijkstra: non-negative weighted shortest path. Bellman-Ford: handles negative edges, detects negative cycles. Floyd-Warshall: all-pairs shortest path O(V^3).

flashcards.front: Inorder traversal of a BST produces?
flashcards.back: Elements in sorted ascending order.

flashcards.front: CPU scheduling: TAT and WT formulas
flashcards.back: Turnaround Time (TAT) = Completion Time - Arrival Time; Waiting Time (WT) = TAT - Burst Time.

flashcards.front: Which scheduling minimizes average waiting time?
flashcards.back: SJF (Shortest Job First) — optimal, but can cause starvation. Round Robin uses a time quantum for fairness/response time.

flashcards.front: Four Coffman deadlock conditions (all must hold)
flashcards.back: (1) Mutual Exclusion, (2) Hold and Wait, (3) No Preemption, (4) Circular Wait. Banker's Algorithm is used for deadlock avoidance.

flashcards.front: External fragmentation — which scheme, and the fix?
flashcards.back: Associated with contiguous memory allocation; fixed by compaction or paging. Paging eliminates external fragmentation but has minor internal fragmentation on the last page.
When the CPU spends more time swapping pages (page faults) than executing instructions, under memory pressure.
Processes have isolated virtual address spaces (heavy context switch); threads within a process share code, heap and open files, keeping only separate stack, registers and Program Counter.
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

flashcards.front: OSI layer of Router vs Switch
flashcards.back: Router operates at Layer 3 (Network); Switch/Bridge at Layer 2 (Data Link).

TCP: reliable, ordered, connection-oriented byte stream (3-way handshake SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK), flow/congestion control. UDP: connectionless datagrams, no delivery/order guarantee, low latency (DNS, DHCP, VoIP).
For a /n mask, host bits h = 32 - n, usable hosts = 2^h - 2 (subtract Network ID and Broadcast ID). Example: /26 -> 2^6 - 2 = 62 hosts.
ARP resolves an IPv4 address to a MAC (link-layer) address; ICMP supports diagnostics/control messages (ping). TTL prevents routing loops.
SMTP (25/587) sends mail; POP3 (110) downloads and typically deletes from the server; IMAP (143) syncs mail across multiple devices.

flashcards.front: IPv4 header field that stops routing loops
flashcards.back: TTL (Time To Live) — each router decrements it by 1 and drops the packet at 0.

flashcards.front: SDLC model with explicit risk analysis every cycle
flashcards.back: Spiral Model (Barry Boehm) — combines iterative development with systematic risk analysis in each loop.

flashcards.front: High cohesion, low coupling golden rule
flashcards.back: Aim for high cohesion (elements inside a module belong together) and low coupling (minimal interdependence between modules).
Black-box = functional (Equivalence Partitioning, Boundary Value Analysis), ignores internal code. White-box = structural (statement/branch/path coverage).

flashcards.front: Smoke vs Sanity vs Regression testing
flashcards.back: Smoke = broad shallow build verification; Sanity = narrow deep check after a minor bug fix; Regression = verify old features didn't break.
Converts the incompatible interface of a legacy (e.g. CBS XML) API into the interface expected by modern clients.
Strategy swaps interchangeable algorithms at runtime (e.g. fee-calculation strategies). Observer = one-to-many event notification (Pub/Sub, Kafka listeners).
Singleton = single shared instance across the JVM (config manager, connection pool). Factory Method = subclasses decide which concrete class to instantiate.
SRP (Single Responsibility), OCP (Open/Closed), LSP (Liskov Substitution), ISP (Interface Segregation), DIP (Dependency Inversion — depend on abstractions, not concretions).
Incident Management restores normal service as quickly as possible (workaround OK). Problem Management finds and eliminates the root cause (RCA); maintains the Known Error Database (KEDB).
Standard (pre-approved low-risk), Normal (requires CAB approval), Emergency (expedited ECAB for critical outages/security patches).
SLA = agreement with external customer/business; OLA = agreement between internal IT teams; UC = Underpinning Contract with external vendors.
SLI = a measured service behaviour; SLO = target for an SLI; SLA = agreement with consequences. Error budget = allowable unreliability under an SLO.
Latency, Traffic, Errors and Saturation.

IaaS: provider manages hardware/virtualization/storage/networking (user manages OS & apps). PaaS: adds OS/runtime/middleware (user deploys code). SaaS: provider manages everything including application & data.
Type 1 (bare-metal) runs directly on hardware (VMware ESXi, KVM, Hyper-V). Type 2 (hosted) runs on top of a host OS (VirtualBox, VMware Workstation).
VMs virtualize hardware with a full guest OS (GBs, slow boot). Containers share the host OS kernel via Linux namespaces (isolation) and cgroups (resource limits) — MBs, millisecond startup.
Image = immutable read-only layered template built from a Dockerfile. Container = running writable instance.

flashcards.front: Dockerfile: COPY vs ADD, ENTRYPOINT vs CMD
flashcards.back: COPY copies local files; ADD also extracts tarballs/URLs. ENTRYPOINT sets a fixed executable; CMD provides overridable default arguments.

flashcards.front: Kubernetes: where is cluster state stored?
flashcards.back: etcd — the distributed, consistent key-value store holding all cluster state.
Pod — one or more containers sharing an IP.
kube-apiserver (REST entry point), etcd (cluster state store), kube-scheduler (assigns Pods to nodes), kube-controller-manager (maintains desired state).
ConfigMap stores non-sensitive config; Secret stores sensitive values (base64/encrypted credentials) and needs cluster encryption/access controls.
Readiness probe decides whether a pod receives traffic; liveness probe detects a stuck/unhealthy container for restart. Misconfigured liveness can cause restart loops.
SAST = static analysis of source/bytecode without running (SonarQube/Checkmarx). DAST = tests the running app externally (OWASP ZAP). SCA = scans third-party dependencies for CVEs (Snyk/Trivy).
Precision = TP / (TP + FP) — of predicted positives, how many are truly positive.
Recall = TP / (TP + FN) — of actual positives, how many were caught (critical in fraud detection).
F1 = 2 x (Precision x Recall) / (Precision + Recall) — the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
Overfitting = high variance (low training error, high test error; fix with L1/L2 regularization, dropout, more data). Underfitting = high bias (high error on both).
Supervised (labelled data: regression & classification), Unsupervised (unlabelled: clustering K-Means, PCA), Reinforcement Learning (agent maximizes cumulative reward).
Controls output randomness/sampling, not factuality: 0 = deterministic/factual, higher = more creative.
Zero-shot (no examples), Few-shot (2-5 examples in prompt), Chain-of-Thought (step-by-step reasoning).

flashcards.front: What is RAG and what does it solve?
flashcards.back: Retrieval-Augmented Generation grounds LLM answers in external documents/vector DBs WITHOUT retraining weights, reducing hallucinations and stale knowledge.
Document ingestion -> chunking -> embedding model (dense vectors) -> vector DB (FAISS, Pinecone, pgvector) -> cosine-similarity retrieval -> augmented prompt -> grounded LLM answer.
RAG adds changing/private knowledge at inference time; fine-tuning changes model parameters/behaviour using training data. They solve different problems and can be combined.
Embeddings are dense numeric vectors encoding semantic meaning; cosine similarity compares vector orientation for retrieval.
Confidentiality (encryption, RBAC), Integrity (hashing SHA-256, HMAC, digital signatures), Availability (redundancy, DDoS protection, DR).
Symmetric (same secret key, fast, bulk data): AES, 3DES, ChaCha20. Asymmetric (public+private key pair, slower, key exchange & signatures): RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman.

Confidentiality: encrypt with receiver's public key, decrypt with receiver's private key. Digital signature: sign the hash with sender's private key, verify with sender's public key (authentication + non-repudiation).
Use salted adaptive password hashing (Argon2/bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2), NOT a plain SHA hash. Hashing is one-way; encryption is reversible.
X.509 is the standard format for public-key digital certificates issued by a CA. TLS 1.3 uses asymmetric crypto for the handshake/key exchange and symmetric AES-GCM for session data.

flashcards.front: OWASP fixes: SQLi, XSS, CSRF, SSRF
flashcards.back: SQL Injection: parameterized/prepared statements. XSS: output encoding + CSP. CSRF: anti-CSRF tokens + SameSite cookies. SSRF: allow-list egress destinations.

flashcards.front: IDS vs IPS vs WAF vs SIEM
flashcards.back: IDS detects & alerts passively; IPS is inline and actively blocks; WAF protects L7 HTTP/API; SIEM centralizes log correlation & SOC alerting.

API1 Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA): access another user's object by changing an identifier. API5 Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA): caller invokes functions/admin endpoints outside their role.
Knowledge (something you know), Possession (something you have), Inherence (something you are). Two passwords are NOT two factors.
RBAC assigns permissions through roles; ABAC evaluates attributes (user, resource, action, environment). Deny by default and verify authorization on every sensitive action.
A security model that grants no implicit trust based on network location; it continuously evaluates context.
RPO (Recovery Point Objective) = maximum acceptable DATA LOSS measured in time. RTO (Recovery Time Objective) = maximum acceptable DOWNTIME to restore service.

flashcards.front: Hot vs Warm vs Cold DR site
flashcards.back: Hot Site: near-zero RTO, live mirrored. Warm Site: hardware ready, periodic backups. Cold Site: empty facility/power only, longest RTO.
ISO 22301 = Business Continuity Management System (BCMS); ISO/IEC 27001 = Information Security Management System (ISMS); PCI-DSS = Payment Card Data Security.
Prepare, detect/analyze, contain, eradicate, recover, learn/post-incident. Preserve evidence and chain of custody.
RBI-operated; 24x7x365 (since 16 Dec 2019); Deferred Net Settlement in 48 half-hourly batches; no RBI minimum or maximum limit.
RBI-operated; real-time gross settlement (no netting); 24x7x365 (since 14 Dec 2020); minimum ₹2,00,000, no upper ceiling. Settlement in RBI books is final and irrevocable.
NPCI-operated; instant, real-time, 24x7x365; up to ₹5,00,000 per transaction; uses Mobile+MMID or Account+IFSC.
NPCI-operated; instant, real-time, 24x7x365; general P2P ₹1 lakh, up to ₹5 lakh for select categories (tax, capital markets, insurance); uses Virtual Payment Address (VPA).
Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (NPCI) — real-time financial inclusion via Aadhaar + biometric/OTP authentication at Micro-ATMs; bank-defined caps.
RBI is India's central bank; it operates NEFT and RTGS. NPCI is the umbrella org for retail payments, operating UPI, IMPS, RuPay, NACH and AePS under RBI oversight.
NPCI-operated National Automated Clearing House for bulk/repetitive transactions — mandates and recurring credits/debits (salaries, subsidies, EMIs).
IFSC = 11-character alphanumeric code (4 bank + 0 + 6 branch). MICR = 9-digit cheque code (3 city + 3 bank + 3 branch).
ISO 8583 = card/ATM switch messaging. ISO 20022 = modern XML financial messaging standard (used by RTGS/SWIFT).
Centralized multi-branch banking ledger system, e.g. Finacle, BaNCS, Flexcube.

flashcards.front: RBI Master Direction on IT Governance effective date
flashcards.back: Issued 7 Nov 2023, effective 1 April 2024. Mandates a Board-level IT Strategy Committee (ITSC), enterprise architecture, capacity management, segregation of duties and periodic DR drills.

flashcards.front: Does a 200 OK response prove a bank transfer settled?
flashcards.back: No. A 200 OK alone does not prove interbank settlement is final; settlement, clearing and reconciliation are separate steps.

flashcards.front: Subject-verb agreement with 'along with / as well as / together with'
flashcards.back: The verb follows the FIRST subject (e.g. 'The manager, along with her engineers, IS reviewing the API').
The verb agrees with the NEAREST subject.
Comprise takes NO 'of' in active voice ('comprises twelve modules', not 'comprises of').
Hardly/Scarcely...WHEN; No sooner...THAN (not 'than' after hardly).
Type 2 = If + past simple, would + base verb. Type 3 = If + had + V3, would have + V3.
Between for two; Among for more than two.

flashcards.front: Relation R(A,B,C,D), candidate key (A,B), FD B -> C: highest normal form?
flashcards.back: 1NF only — B -> C is a partial dependency (C depends on part of the composite key), violating 2NF.

cheatsheets.title: HTTP Status Codes
items: 200 OK — successful request
201 Created — resource created (Location header may identify it)
202 Accepted — accepted for processing, completion not yet guaranteed
204 No Content — success with no response body
400 Bad Request — malformed request
401 Unauthorized — missing/invalid authentication
403 Forbidden — authenticated but lacks permission
404 Not Found — resource does not exist
409 Conflict — request conflicts with current state
412 Precondition Failed
429 Too Many Requests — rate limit exceeded
500 Internal Server Error
502 Bad Gateway — invalid response from upstream server
503 Service Unavailable
504 Gateway Timeout

cheatsheets.title: HTTP Methods: Safe & Idempotent
items: GET — safe, idempotent; read resource, cacheable; returns 200 or 404
HEAD — safe, idempotent; like GET but no response body (metadata checks)
POST — not safe, not idempotent; create/trigger action; returns 201 (use Idempotency-Key in payments)
PUT — not safe, idempotent; full replacement; returns 200 or 204
PATCH — not safe, not guaranteed idempotent; partial update
DELETE — not safe, idempotent; repeated calls leave the same server state

cheatsheets.title: Common Port Numbers
items: SSH — 22
Telnet — 23
SMTP — 25 (submission 587)
DNS — 53
HTTP — 80
NTP — 123
IMAP — 143
HTTPS — 443
MQTT — 1883
MySQL — 3306
PostgreSQL — 5432
Redis — 6379
HTTP alternate/application — 8080 (not a universal standard)

cheatsheets.title: OSI Layers & Protocols
items: Layer 1 Physical — Bits; Hub, Repeater; cables, fiber, Wi-Fi signals
Layer 2 Data Link — Frame; Switch, Bridge; Ethernet (48-bit MAC), VLAN 802.1Q, PPP, CSMA/CD
Layer 3 Network — Packet; Router; IPv4 (32-bit), IPv6 (128-bit), ICMP, ARP, OSPF, BGP; TTL prevents loops
Layer 4 Transport — Segment; Firewall; TCP (connection-oriented 3-way handshake) vs UDP (connectionless)
Layers 5-7 Session/Presentation/Application — Data; Gateway; HTTP, HTTPS, SSH, FTP, SMTP, DNS, POP3, IMAP
Routers operate at Layer 3; switches at Layer 2

cheatsheets.title: Sorting & DSA Complexities
items: Quick Sort — avg O(n log n), worst O(n^2), space O(log n); unstable
Merge Sort — O(n log n) all cases, space O(n); stable, good for linked lists/external sort
Heap Sort — O(n log n), space O(1); in-place, unstable
Counting/Radix/Bucket — O(n + k); non-comparison, beats O(n log n) lower bound
Binary Search — O(log n); requires sorted/monotonic input
Array indexed access — O(1); middle insert/delete O(n)
Hash table lookup — average O(1), worst O(n)
Balanced BST search/insert — O(log n); inorder traversal is sorted
Heap peek — O(1); insert/remove top O(log n)
BFS/DFS — O(V+E); BFS finds shortest path in unweighted graphs
Floyd-Warshall all-pairs shortest path — O(V^3)

cheatsheets.title: SQL Command Classification (DDL/DML/DCL/TCL)
items: DDL (schema, auto-committed) — CREATE, ALTER, DROP, TRUNCATE, RENAME
DML (data rows, rollback-able) — SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, MERGE
DCL (permissions) — GRANT, REVOKE
TCL (transactions) — COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT
DELETE — DML, supports WHERE, logs each row, fires triggers, rollback-able
TRUNCATE — DDL, removes all rows fast, resets auto-increment, no WHERE
DROP — removes both data and table structure

cheatsheets.title: SQL Isolation Levels & Anomalies
items: READ UNCOMMITTED — allows Dirty, Non-Repeatable and Phantom Reads
READ COMMITTED — prevents Dirty Reads; allows Non-Repeatable & Phantom (PostgreSQL/Oracle default)
REPEATABLE READ — prevents Dirty & Non-Repeatable Reads (MySQL InnoDB default; gap locks also prevent phantoms)
SERIALIZABLE — prevents all three; highest isolation, lowest concurrency
Dirty Read — reading another transaction's uncommitted change
Non-Repeatable Read — same row read twice yields different committed values
Phantom Read — re-running a predicate query returns a changed set of rows

cheatsheets.title: Normalization Forms (1NF to BCNF)
items: 1NF — atomic cells only; no multi-valued or composite attributes
2NF — 1NF + no partial dependency (non-prime attr on part of a composite key); auto-satisfied if PK is a single column
3NF — 2NF + no transitive dependency; for X -> Y, X is a superkey OR Y is a prime attribute
BCNF — for EVERY non-trivial FD X -> Y, X must be a superkey/candidate key
Denormalization — intentionally duplicates/precomputes data for read performance at the cost of write complexity

cheatsheets.title: ACID Properties & Indexing
items: Atomicity — all-or-nothing; debit from A must credit B, else full rollback
Consistency — preserves DB invariants/constraints
Isolation — concurrent transactions do not interfere
Durability — committed data survives crash via Write-Ahead Logging (WAL)
B+ Tree index — supports range queries (BETWEEN, <, >, ORDER BY); default in PostgreSQL/MySQL/Oracle
Hash index — exact equality (=) only, O(1)
Clustered index — at most ONE per table, sets physical row order (usually PK)
Composite index leftmost-prefix — index on (a,b,c) helps a or a,b, NOT b,c alone
Functions on indexed columns (WHERE YEAR(dt)=2026) break index usage

cheatsheets.title: Payment System Limits (UPI/NEFT/RTGS/IMPS)
items: NEFT — RBI; 24x7x365; Deferred Net Settlement in 48 half-hourly batches; no min/max limit
RTGS — RBI; real-time gross settlement; 24x7x365; minimum ₹2,00,000, no upper ceiling; final & irrevocable
IMPS — NPCI; instant 24x7x365; up to ₹5,00,000 per transaction; Mobile+MMID or Account+IFSC
UPI — NPCI; instant 24x7x365; general P2P ₹1 lakh, up to ₹5 lakh for select categories (tax, capital markets, insurance)
AePS — NPCI; Aadhaar + biometric/OTP at Micro-ATMs; bank-defined caps
NACH — NPCI; bulk/repetitive mandates (salaries, subsidies, EMIs)
RuPay — NPCI domestic card network

cheatsheets.title: Cloud Service Models
items: IaaS — provider manages hardware, virtualization, servers, storage, networking; user manages OS & apps (AWS EC2, Azure VMs, GCP Compute Engine)
PaaS — IaaS + OS, runtime, middleware; user deploys code (AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Heroku, Google App Engine)
SaaS — provider manages everything including application & data (Gmail, Salesforce, Microsoft 365)
DBaaS/BaaS — managed database provisioning, patching, backups (Google Firebase, AWS RDS, MongoDB Atlas)
Type 1 hypervisor (bare-metal) — VMware ESXi, KVM, Hyper-V
Type 2 hypervisor (hosted) — VirtualBox, VMware Workstation

cheatsheets.title: Kubernetes Objects & Architecture
items: Pod — smallest deployable unit; 1+ containers sharing an IP
Deployment — declarative stateless replicas & rolling updates
StatefulSet — stable identity/storage ordering
DaemonSet — runs a pod on selected nodes; Job/CronJob run finite/scheduled tasks
Service — stable virtual IP (ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer)
Ingress — HTTP/HTTPS L7 routing
ConfigMap — non-sensitive config; Secret — sensitive values (base64/encrypted)
PersistentVolumeClaim — requests persistent storage
Control Plane — kube-apiserver, etcd (cluster state), kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager
Worker Node — kubelet, kube-proxy, container runtime (containerd)

cheatsheets.title: GoF Design Patterns
items: Singleton (creational) — single shared instance across JVM (config manager, connection pool)
Factory Method (creational) — subclasses decide which concrete class to instantiate
Builder (creational) — construct complex immutable objects step-by-step
Adapter (structural) — convert an incompatible legacy interface to the expected one
Decorator (structural) — add behaviour dynamically (Java I/O streams)
Proxy (structural) — control access (Spring AOP, caching)
Strategy (behavioral) — swap interchangeable algorithms at runtime
Observer (behavioral) — one-to-many event notification (Pub/Sub, Kafka)
Repository — abstracts persistence; Circuit Breaker — stops calls to a failing dependency

cheatsheets.title: ITIL / ITSM Concepts
items: Incident Management — restore normal service as quickly as possible (workaround OK)
Problem Management — find & eliminate root cause (RCA); maintains Known Error Database (KEDB)
Change Enablement — Standard (pre-approved), Normal (CAB approval), Emergency (ECAB)
Service Request — predefined user request, standard fulfilment
SLA — agreement with external customer/business
OLA — agreement between internal IT teams
UC — Underpinning Contract with external vendors
CMDB — stores Configuration Items (CIs) and their dependencies
CAB — Change Advisory Board advises on change assessment/authorization
SLI measured behaviour / SLO target / SLA agreement with consequences; error budget = allowable unreliability

cheatsheets.title: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023)
items: API1 Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA) — access another user's object by changing an identifier
API2 Broken Authentication — weak auth/session/token handling
API3 Broken Object Property Level Authorization — exposes/modifies properties beyond entitlement
API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption — no limits on compute/storage/bandwidth
API5 Broken Function Level Authorization — invoking functions/admin endpoints outside role
API6 Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows — automated abuse of sensitive flows
API7 Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
API8 Security Misconfiguration — unsafe defaults, CORS, verbose errors
API9 Improper Inventory Management — shadow/old API versions
API10 Unsafe Consumption of APIs — trusting third-party responses without validation

cheatsheets.title: Cryptography & Security Controls
items: CIA triad — Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability
Symmetric (same secret key, fast) — AES (128/192/256), 3DES, ChaCha20
Asymmetric (public+private pair, slower) — RSA, ECC, Diffie-Hellman
Confidentiality — encrypt with receiver's public key, decrypt with private key
Digital signature — sign hash with sender's private key, verify with public key (non-repudiation)
Hashing (SHA-256) is one-way; store passwords with salted Argon2/bcrypt/scrypt/PBKDF2
X.509 — public-key certificate format issued by a CA; revocation via CRL/OCSP
TLS 1.3 — asymmetric handshake + symmetric AES-GCM for session data
IDS detects/alerts; IPS inline blocks; WAF L7 protection; SIEM log correlation
OWASP fixes — SQLi: prepared statements; XSS: output encoding + CSP; CSRF: tokens + SameSite; SSRF: egress allow-list

cheatsheets.title: BCP/DR Metrics & Standards
items: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) — maximum acceptable data loss measured in time
RTO (Recovery Time Objective) — maximum acceptable downtime to restore service
BIA (Business Impact Analysis) — identifies critical activities, dependencies and impact over time
Hot Site — near-zero RTO, live mirrored
Warm Site — hardware ready, periodic backups
Cold Site — empty facility/power only, longest RTO
ISO 22301 — Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
ISO/IEC 27001 — Information Security Management System (ISMS)
PCI-DSS — Payment Card Data Security
Replication reduces RPO but cannot replace tested backups

cheatsheets.title: ML Metrics & Formula Bank
items: Precision = TP / (TP + FP)
Recall = TP / (TP + FN)
F1 = 2 x Precision x Recall / (Precision + Recall)
Availability = Uptime / (Uptime + Downtime) x 100%
99.9% availability ~ 43.2 minutes downtime in a 30-day month (approximation)
Subnet usable hosts = 2^(32-n) - 2
TAT = Completion Time - Arrival Time; WT = TAT - Burst Time
Overfitting = high variance (fix: regularization, dropout, more data); Underfitting = high bias
Supervised (labelled), Unsupervised (clustering/PCA), Reinforcement (reward maximization)

cheatsheets.title: Banking & IT Glossary Essentials
items: ACID — Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
Idempotency — multiple identical requests produce the same state as one
CBS — Core Banking Solution (centralized bank ledger)
IFSC — 11-char Indian Financial System Code (4 bank + 0 + 6 branch)
MICR — 9-digit Magnetic Ink Character Recognition cheque code
ISO 8583 — card/ATM switch messaging; ISO 20022 — modern XML financial messaging
JWT — JSON Web Token (Header.Payload.Signature), signed not encrypted
WAL — Write-Ahead Log for database recovery
VPA — Virtual Payment Address (UPI); TPAP — Third-Party Application Provider
Zero Trust — no implicit trust based on network location

cheatsheets.title: OS & Networking Must-Knows
items: Deadlock (Coffman, all 4) — mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no preemption, circular wait
Banker's Algorithm — deadlock avoidance via safe-state checks
SJF minimizes average waiting time (can starve); Round Robin uses a time quantum
External fragmentation — contiguous allocation; fixed by compaction or paging
Thrashing — CPU spends more time swapping pages than executing
Process has isolated address space; threads share code/heap/files, separate stack & PC
TCP — reliable ordered connection-oriented; UDP — connectionless, low latency
DNS resolves names; DHCP leases IP config; ARP resolves IPv4 to MAC; ICMP diagnostics
